text: This chunk details the symptoms of German measles (Rubella), distinguishing between infections in children and adults, and infections in fetuses from their mothers. It describes the pre-rash and rash stages, noting that about 50% of cases are asymptomatic. The pre-rash symptoms include mild fever, headache, and swollen lymph nodes, while the rash is characterized by small, pink, flat spots that spread from the face down to the body over 1-3 days. The text also highlights potential congenital defects in fetuses, such as deafness, heart defects, and cataracts, if the mother contracts the virus during pregnancy.
